caption:
Tesla's Grok AI can now text anyone in your phone as you, just from your voice inside the car. Nobody announced it.

Until this week, your Tesla's voice assistant handled music and directions. Your contacts were yours alone. That just changed. Grok, Elon Musk's AI, can now compose and send a text to anyone in your phone just from your voice, as you. No typing. The manual does not describe any confirmation step.

There was no launch event. No press release. Someone found it buried in an updated Model Y owner's manual PDF and posted it on X. That's how the world found out Grok now has full access to your entire contact list.

Every Tesla owner's boss, family, and ex is now reachable by an AI that speaks as you. The post exposing it hit 99.7K views within hours of going up.

This is the first time a car's AI has been able to write and send a text as you, in your voice, without you ever announcing it as a feature.

Cars are becoming platforms where AI can act on your behalf. Tesla has said nothing.

Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.

Sources: cb_doge on X, Tesla Model Y Owner's Manual

story.title: BREAKING: Tesla drivers will soon be able to text using Grok. The updated Model Y owner manual says drivers will be able to ask Grok to text any contact or phone number by voice.

editor_override: Caption sentence 'This is the first time a car's AI has been able to write and send a text as you, in your voice, without you ever announcing it as a feature' contains a Truth Law violation: the 'first ever' claim is too broad — Siri via CarPlay has sent voice-composed texts from cars for years. Scope it to what is actually new and verifiable: a car's built-in AI composing and sending texts in you
